name: agent_recv
description: Receive pending mailbox messages for this session, waiting (parked at this session's runner) up to the bounded timeout when none are pending. A child parked here yields its execution slot. Delivery is at-least-once: unconsumed deliveries are re-delivered after a crash, deduped on message_id. One receive is live per session: a newer call supersedes an older parked one, and the superseded call completes SUCCESSFULLY with no messages and a `disposition` saying it yielded — nothing was lost, do not retry it. On timeout the call fails with no message and its error says what to do next.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for a message (default 60, max 600); on timeout the call fails with no message and its error says what to do next

disposition.description: Set only when this call yielded to a newer receive for the same session: a successful receive that delivered nothing and must not be retried. Absent on a delivering receive.

items.description: Inbound relayed message from a sibling (or the coordinator itself, from_agent_id == ""). Reply via PeerSendRequest.in_reply_to. Until delivered, a queued PeerMessage is durable, role-addressed mailbox state at the coordinator: it survives coordinator process restarts and is delivered when the target reattaches.

kind.description: The message's kind, from a CLOSED vocabulary — guaranteed to be one of these names, because an unrecognised value is refused at ingress rather than delivered unclassified. A SENDER could only have set one of MESSAGE_KIND_MESSAGE, MESSAGE_KIND_RESULT, MESSAGE_KIND_ERROR, MESSAGE_KIND_QUESTION; the rest are minted by the coordinator itself and are therefore trustworthy as to provenance. MESSAGE_KIND_USER_INJECTED means a human injected text into a session you supervise; MESSAGE_KIND_EXITED means a child of yours ended; MESSAGE_KIND_USER_CONTROL and MESSAGE_KIND_STEER are control-plane notices.

structured.description: Structured companion the sender attached, when there is one. This object no longer carries the message kind — read the `kind` field.
